about: Curated golden set for Forge3D v3.0 Phase 6 (C3): 60 corpus cases selected from tests/native/corpus.json by a deterministic rule -- (1) the shortest case exercising each diagnostic code in corpus.json's baked 'codes' fields (17 codes: E101 E102 E103 E104 E110 E201 E202 E204 E205 E301 E302 E303 E401 E402 E501 E820 W101), (2) up to two shortest build-bearing cases per feature family (geometry, materials, lights, env, keys, particles, post, shader, skin, sprites/text, gltf/obj, cameras; family = keyword match on src), (3) filled to 60 with the shortest remaining build cases, then the shortest remaining cases. Case objects are copied byte-for-byte from corpus.json (schema: src / check / optional build, identical to corpus.json); 'corpus_indices' lists the original corpus index of each case, in ascending order. The selection rule lives in this 'about' field because the corpus schema's only metadata field is 'about'.

cases.src:
Tests for the Forge3D validator (tools/f3dc/validate.py).

Stdlib ``unittest`` only; standalone-runnable::

    python3 tests/compiler/test_validate.py

Programs are built through the real front end -- ``parser.parse`` feeds
``validate.validate(program, bag, base_dir='.')``, which returns an
``IRScene`` on success and ``None`` iff the error bag holds an error.
Error-code families follow validate.py: E201 names/targets, E202 colour,
E204 texture, E205 not-built-yet, E301 object/scene dimensions,
E302 camera/light ranges, E303 animation/output timing, E501 missing file.

The validate triangle estimate for one compiled IR object.

    The props are the object's normalised geometry payload (the same
    dict ``validate`` folds into its E820 estimate), so this is the
    compiler's own estimate for the object as compiled, checked here
    against the closed-form Fortran formula per primitive.  The
    ``ext_geometry`` entry point (which ``validate`` delegates to for
    the Wave D prims) must agree exactly.
